title: Where is Happiness?
paragraphs: Though the feeling of pleasure is common to all living beings, it is, in particular, that special feeling felt by man and woman united together.

Iḷampūraṇar elaborates on it stating that even a natural instinct like happiness requires union of hearts. He points out that, if good rapport exists, one can experience pleasure significantly even in the company of a prostitute. But in the absence of good rapport, one cannot derive joy even from his wife.

While explaining the term “all living beings,” Nacciṉārkkiṉiyar makes it clear that happiness experienced by male and female in union is common to all living creatures - people, gods, demons, animals and birds.

When Nacciṉārkkiṉiyar brings in the celestials and the demons while referring to all living beings, one cannot be oblivious of the fact that the purānas abound in stories of male gods taking the female form and enjoying sex with the male beings.

As such, we need to steer clear of the joy of union belonging to the worlds of harlots and gods and must look at the Tolkāppiyam verse with reference to the human male and human female united by mutual love. This alone goes in accord with Tamil culture.
> Joy is > The joy of union between the sexes > That every living being accomplishes > As it unites in passion with its loving mate.
